speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to begin my assessment, could you describe exactly how your walking difficulties have progressed over time and what triggers them?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description of appearing "drunk" while walking suggests significant ataxia. You mentioned feeling clumsy specifically on the right side; is this asymmetry constant, or does it worsen in certain situations like standing still or when you are stressed?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. I need to confirm this by reviewing your neurological exam findings and ordering an MRI of your brain to look for non-enhancing white matter lesions.
